title: Complete directed Hamiltonian cycle thresholds proof

insights: list_path_to_hamiltonian: build equivalence from l.getElem, prove bijective via Nodup + full coverage
Surjectivity: List.mem_iff_getElem + hmem (∀ v, v ∈ l from Finset.eq_univ_of_card)
Arc condition: Equiv.ofBijective preserves function values, so σ.symm i = l[i]
sc_tournament_has_cycle: proved via back arc contradiction on Hamiltonian path
Back arc argument: if no l[j]→l[i] arc exists (j>i), then l[n-1] has no outgoing arcs, contradicting SC (path l[n-1]→l[0] must start with an arc)
Cycle from back arc: C = (l.drop i).take (j-i+1) with wrap arc l[j]→l[i]; Nodup from list.drop.take; length from omega
tournament_cycle_non_insertable: proved via successor closure - arc(l[i],u) → arc(l[(i+1)%k],u) by tournament property; forward iteration gives all-or-none
list_cycle_to_hamiltonian: proved analogously to list_path_to_hamiltonian (Equiv.ofBijective, modular index matching)
grow_cycle_to_hamiltonian: proved by induction on deficit n-k, using tournament_cycle_extendable at each step
moon_moser statement proved (depends on tournament_cycle_extendable which is still sorry)
redei theorem fully proved via tournament_full_path_list + list_path_to_hamiltonian
nextSteps: tournament_cycle_extendable (line 490): key remaining sorry - S+/S- partition argument
Proof: pick u not in C; either insert u (done) or u non-insertable (all-or-none)
If all C beats u: S- set; SC gives path S-→C; but no arc S-→C → contradiction
If u beats all C: S+ set; SC gives path C→S+; but no arc C→S+ → contradiction
When both S+, S- exist: find b∈S-, a∈S+ with arc b→a; form longer cycle → contradicts maximality
ghouila_houri (line 300): deep directed Dirac theorem, likely needs its own approach
directed_hamiltonian_threshold (line 590): reduce to moon_moser via degree argument
